Header:

Transcript:
[00:00] Ariela: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. I'm Ariela, AE at Redwood, and with me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Mark: Good, thanks. Mark here, CTO at East Bank. We'll keep it tight 30-ish minutes.
[00:10] Rachel: Rachel here. Security lead. I mainly want to understand data flows and logging retention.
[00:14] Tom: Tom, infra. I'll ask about networking and on-prem options.
[00:17] Ariela: Great, our objective today is to understand your residency and compliance constraints — GDPR, HIPAA, financial regs — and map Redwood hosted/dedicated/private options to those needs.
[00:25] Samir: Quick note, I'll jump in for technical bits; apologies in advance for any audio fuzz, we got a slightly noisy connection.
[00:30] Mark: Quick background — East Bank is rolling out an LLM assistant for internal ops and a treasury product that may touch health-adjacent data (small amount in some customer notes), so we need to be careful about HIPAA scope. Primarily, our regulatory ask is EU data residency for EU customers, strict logging controls for audits, and retention windows we can configure. We want to evaluate Redwood Hosted first but need to know if Dedicated or Private are required for compliance.
[00:58] Ariela: Understood. In general, Redwood Hosted keeps compute in the region chosen, but for strict residency and control we usually recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools in a customer-specific tenant with tenancy isolation and dedicated VPC peering options; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options.
[01:20] Rachel: Can you explain what "compute in the region" exactly means? If we choose hosted EU region, does data ever leave EU for things like logging or monitoring?
[01:28] Samir: Good q. Hosted EU-region keeps inference requests and model execution in the selected region, but some control-plane metadata and aggregated telemetry may be ingested into Redwood's control plane in the US unless you opt for Private. For customers with strict residency we provide options: 1) Dedicated with regional-only telemetry retention and contractual terms, or 2) Private where control plane can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem so logs never leave. I'll caveat that our standard Hosted tier uses global observability by default.
[01:58] Rachel: So Hosted is not acceptable for us if logs need to stay in EU.
[02:02] Mark: Yeah, for enterprise EU customers we need proof that logs and any PII never cross borders without consent.
[02:08] Ariela: Totally, we see that. On Dedicated we can offer region-bound audit logs, KMS integration in the customer's region, and contractual clauses for data residency. For full control we recommend Private where the control plane and audit logs are wholly customer-managed.
[02:25] Tom: Technical Q: networking — do you support VPC peering and can we get a private link? We need no public egress from our subnets.
[02:33] Samir: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private connectivity. For Private we can deploy into your VPC so there is zero public egress. With Hosted we offer private link in some regions but it's less common for strict-regulated deployments. Also, for Dedicated we can bump up encryption at rest with CMKs and integrate with your HSM if needed.
[02:54] Rachel: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with retention controls and the ability to produce them for auditors. How granular are the logs? Do you log prompts and responses?
[03:03] Ariela: Default is that request metadata, model version, latency, and aggregated token metrics are logged. Prompt/response logging is opt-in. For customers with strict controls we have a mode where prompt/response are not stored or are stored encrypted with the customer's KMS and with short retention windows.
[03:21] Rachel: And the opt-in storage — is that documented for HIPAA purposes? We need BAAs and to know how you handle ePHI.
[03:28] Samir: Redwood does HIPAA support for Private and certain Dedicated engagements; we sign a BAA and our security pack includes ePHI handling guidelines. Hosted has limited HIPAA coverage — typically Dedicated or Private.
[03:43] Mark: For GDPR, we also need evidence of data subject access handling and deletion workflows — if someone requests data deletion, how do we ensure it's scrubbed from caches/KV caches etc?
[03:53] Samir: Great point. We have tenant-level KV cache controls and TTLs; in Dedicated/Private you get the ability to clear caches on demand and we support purge APIs you can call. For Hosted there's a standard retention policy and purge paths but tighter SLAs around deletion are part of Dedicated/Private contracts.
[04:10] Lisa: From product side, latency is important — if we go on-prem vs hosted, what's the latency diff? We care about 50–150ms token latency target for live assistant.
[04:18] Samir: Latency largely depends on model choice and physical proximity. Hosted in eu-west-1 with optimized kernels gets best latency for EU users; Dedicated in eu-west-1 will be comparable but gives you isolation. Private on-prem reduces network hop but you trade off having to run and maintain infra — also model variants may need different quantization which can alter latency. We can run benchmarks as part of the POC.
[04:41] Mark: On cost — Dedicated vs Hosted — what's the expected delta? We may be sensitive to unit costs for heavy token volumes.
[04:48] Ariela: In short, Dedicated has a commit/reserved pricing model which lowers per-token cost at scale, plus predictable throughput. Hosted is pay-as-you-go and more flexible but higher marginal costs. Private tends to be a license + ops cost. We'll share a sample pricing sheet.
[05:03] Rachel: A few more compliance items: SSO/SAML support for RBAC, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC for data export; plus encryption key control.
[05:12] Samir: All supported: SAML SSO, SCIM, and RBAC are standard for Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports SSO too but enterprise features are stronger in Dedicated. KMS integrations for CMEK supported in Dedicated/Private.
[05:25] Tom: If we choose Private, is there an option for air-gapped on-prem? We have some regulated customers requiring that.
[05:30] Samir: Yes, we offer an on-prem package for Private deployments. That includes a deployable control plane and inference runtime. Air-gapped setups are possible but come with longer lead times and support SLAs. We usually run an initial staging deploy in a connected environment then help harden for air-gap.
[05:47] Lisa: Can you run through the typical pathway you see banks take? Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private?
[05:52] Ariela: Often customers start with Hosted for initial experiments, then move to Dedicated when they need predictable throughput and stronger contractual commitments. Private is chosen for the strictest compliance/residency cases. But some financial institutions go directly to Dedicated or Private depending on audit timelines.
[06:07] Mark: We likely need Dedicated for the pilot with possibility to move to Private if auditors push back. Our timeline: pilot Q4 2026, production H1 2027.
[06:16] Ariela: That timing aligns well. We'll scope a Dedicated pilot and include the audit controls you listed.
[06:21] Rachel: A few specifics to include in docs: 1) Data residency contract language for EU-only processing, 2) BAA template for ePHI, 3) Log retention and deletion API details, 4) KMS/HSM integration notes.
[06:35] Ariela: We'll send a security bundle covering those. Samir, I'll let you note the technical follow-ups.
[06:40] Samir: Action items — I'll prepare an initial architecture sketch showing Dedicated VPC peering, KMS integration (customer CMKs), and options for encrypted prompt logging vs no logging. Also I'll prepare a latency/cost estimate for eu-west-1 Dedicated with typical batching settings.
[06:55] Tom: For the architecture sketch, can you include the fallback behavior — e.g., if Dedicated capacity saturated do you auto-fallback to hosted? We need strict availability without violating residency.
[07:04] Samir: Good catch. We support routing policies; for strict residency you'd disable cross-region fallback. For availability we can configure canary capacity in another EU zone or reserved burst capacity. We'll call out explicit policies in the diagram.
[07:18] Mark: We also need to know about logging restrictions — in particular we cannot send raw prompts containing PII to any third-party unless encrypted. So any telemetry/monitored data must be scrubbed.
[07:28] Ariela: We offer prompt scrubbing, token-level redaction, and a configured pipeline to avoid logging sensitive fields. For Dedicated we'll work with you on a scrub list and regexes.
[07:38] Rachel: One last legal process Q — procurement wants to know if Redwood accepts standard bank redlines on data residency clauses or do you require your template?
[07:46] Ariela: We typically start with Redwood's template but are open to negotiating residency clauses and SLAs for enterprise/Dedicated deals. Private deployments are easiest for customers who need custom legal terms.
[07:56] Mark: Good. Last thing: can you confirm SOC2 and whether you have ISO certifications?
[08:01] Ariela: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO 27001 in progress; I'll include the attestations in the pack.
[08:09] Lisa: OK sounds good. Next steps recap?
[08:12] Ariela: Recap — send security + SOC2/BAA, Dedicated pricing, schedule deep dive next week for infra, and East Bank to send compliance matrix. Any objections?
[08:22] Mark: None. We'll circulate internal stakeholders after the deck.
[08:25] Rachel: Thanks. If you can highlight HIPAA coverage for ePHI in Dedicated/Private that'd be great.
[08:31] Ariela: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
[08:35] Tom: Thanks, bye.

(End of call)
